dedupe_keys.name: usmin prospect and mine related features from usgs topographic maps

description: The USMIN Mineral Deposit Database Project of the U.S. Geological Survey, based at the Geology, Geophysics, and Geochemistry Science Center in Denver, develops national geospatial databases of the most significant mines, mineral deposits and mining districts of the United States, to support land-use planning, hazard evaluation and resource assessment. Its main data release digitises symbols of mining-related features from historical USGS topographic quadrangle maps, which carried such symbols from the late 1800s through 2006: prospect pits, mine shafts and adits, quarries, open-pit mines, tailings piles and ponds, and gravel and borrow pits, with the source map for each feature. Version 10.0 (May 2023) is published as a USGS data release (doi:10.5066/F78W3CHG), with a consolidated version (doi:10.5066/P9TAALR6); both are free public-domain downloads. Caveats: coverage was built state by state, starting with the western conterminous United States, the features reflect the date of each historical map, not current status, and many are small prospects. For simulation it gives the locations of mine openings and mine waste for hazard exposure studies, for example subsidence or tailings near roads, pipelines and water supplies. Related catalogue records include the USGS Mineral Resources Data System, which USMIN succeeds for the United States.
